chapter: Childhood, first drums and the hustling years
title: Born in Memphis, moving to Chicago in 1923, raised by his sister
summary: Saunders was born in Memphis in 1912, lost his mother in 1919, and was raised by his much older sister, who moved the family to Chicago for work and passed for white.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay, let's start at the beginning. When and where were you born?
Yeah, well, I was born in Memphis, Tennessee on March 2, 1912. Yeah, so --
When did you move to Chicago?
Well, I moved to Chicago in 1923.
When you were 11 years old.
Yeah, right.
Your family came up here.
Yeah, well, my sister raised me, you know. Earlier, my mother died, in 1919, and then my father, he left us and my sister raised me. So she became my mother and father.
How many were in your family?
There was six of us, two girls and four boys. Now, we have only one brother left, so now -- and it's he and I, you know.
Were you the youngest or -- ?
I was the youngest, right, right. And my brother is the oldest boy. And this home here is -- was my sister's and for the last three years, I -- four years, in
fact, I raised -- I took care of her until she passed, about a year and a half ago.
Why did you all move to Chicago? For work?
Well, it was for working conditions, yeah. And I was a youngster, and my sister brought my younger sister and myself here and she raised us, and then she went to work here, you know.
Let's see, and that was '23.

That was in 1923, and she was very, very light-completed, and she worked -- during those times, they weren't like they are now. So she passed -- you know, they call it passing, she passed for white. She passed for white for -- oh, I guess up until about 1940, from that time, over 20-some years, 25 years. And she raised me and sent me to Milwaukee to boarding school there, and my other sister grew up to get a job.
And so, we had been very close ever since. She was like a mother, like I said before, to me.
How much older was she?
Well, when she passed she was 79 years old. And that was two years ago. So she would have been 81 now.
So she was about 16 years older than you.
